reply:
**Uri Simonsohn** is a behavioral scientist and methodologist whose work focuses on judgment and decision-making, research methods, and the credibility and reproducibility of empirical findings. He is especially known for developing and applying statistical techniques to detect questionable research practices and for coauthoring influential work on **false-positive psychology**, **p-hacking**, and **specification-curve analysis**. ([urisohn.com](https://urisohn.com/about/))

### Recent research news

The most prominent recent attention around Simonsohn has come through **Data Colada**, the research blog he runs with Joseph Simmons and Leif Nelson:

- In **August–September 2026**, Simonsohn and collaborators published posts arguing that an influential study on procrastination and deadlines by Dan Ariely and Klaus Wertenbroch showed evidence of fraud, following a failed replication and examination of the study’s underlying files. ([datacolada.urisohn.com](https://www.datacolada.urisohn.com/))
- He has also recently coauthored a commentary challenging a 2025 paper’s conclusion about the **gambler’s fallacy**, arguing that a different analysis of the data provides evidence that biased beliefs do contribute to the effect. ([papers.ssrn.com](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=7441481))
- More broadly, his public profile is associated with using statistical reanalysis to scrutinize influential behavioral-science findings and improve research transparency.

### What he teaches at Yale SOM

The SOM course catalog currently lists Simonsohn as teaching:

- **MGMT 7307 — Method Stumblers Part 1**
  - **Instructor:** Uri Simonsohn  
  - **Category:** PhD  
  - **Units:** 0.5  
  - **Meeting:** Wednesdays, 4:10–7:10 p.m.  
  - **Room:** Evans 4210  
  - **Session:** Fall 1, September 2–October 16, 2026  

The catalog describes it as covering “analytical tools and topics that have not been discussed in previous operations doctoral courses,” with emphasis on modeling and analyzing operational processes. It also identifies Simonsohn as a **Visiting Professor of Behavioral Science at Yale SOM for the 2026–27 academic year**.
